parts: network models for power, water and transport

subsystems.name: Validation and governance layer
subsystems.role: keeps the output honest and lawful.

buildSteps.title: Fix the question
buildSteps.detail: Decide what decision the simulation must inform and which outcomes count as success, before any code is written.

buildSteps.title: Build the geospatial base
buildSteps.detail: Fuse remote sensing, cadastral records and utility maps into one consistent three-dimensional model of buildings, parcels, roads and networks.

buildSteps.title: Generate a synthetic population
buildSteps.detail: Create individual households and firms with attributes drawn from census microdata, reweighted until district-level totals match published statistics.

buildSteps.title: Encode behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Write decision rules for each agent type; where language models are used, prompt them with a persona, an income, a location and the constraints of the proposed rule, and check their choices against observed behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and backtest
buildSteps.detail: Replay a policy that already happened, or a shock such as a fuel price rise, and tune the model until it reproduces the real outcome within stated error bars.

buildSteps.title: Run scenarios
buildSteps.detail: Apply the proposed rule as a parameter change and run many randomised replicates, producing distributions of outcomes rather than a single headline number.

buildSteps.title: Audit and report
buildSteps.detail: Test whether the model penalises particular groups, quantify how much the answer depends on contested assumptions, and publish uncertainty ranges a non-modeller can read.

prerequisites.why: long-established methods for simulating many interacting decision-makers, already used in tax, transport and epidemic planning.

prerequisites.tech: City-scale digital twins with high-resolution data
prerequisites.why: national and municipal twins exist as pilots and platforms, but coverage and currency vary widely.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models as behavioural proxies
prerequisites.why: demonstrated in research that they can approximate survey responses, but they carry known biases and drift from real populations.
cloud clusters make large ensemble runs feasible, though cost scales with the number of replicates needed for credible uncertainty.

prerequisites.tech: Validation data and causal inference methods
prerequisites.why: without reliable evidence on how real people responded to past rules, a simulation is unfalsifiable.

pathway.milestone: digital twins of cities and regions used for transport, energy and environmental planning
pathway.unlocks: a tested geospatial and network backbone that policy models can stand on.

pathway.milestone: synthetic populations coupled to language-model agents, calibrated to surveys and elections
pathway.unlocks: rapid pre-testing of proposed rules across many assumed behaviours.

pathway.milestone: regulators formally accepting ensemble policy simulations as one input to impact assessment
pathway.unlocks: fewer unintended consequences, provided uncertainty is reported rather than hidden.

pathway.milestone: audited, contestable twins that citizens and researchers can inspect and challenge
pathway.unlocks: legitimacy for decisions informed by simulation, without pretending the model is the public.
